Subject: Throughput SLO for Reserved Pool — request for assurance

Hi Michael / Lauren,

Thanks again for the walkthrough this morning. We’re moving toward a pilot that will process clinical transcripts in near-real-time and the downstream SLA with our provider requires us to demonstrate a 99th-percentile throughput envelope under production traffic. Currently our procurement team is asking for stronger contractual language around dedicated pool throughput and queueing behavior (they call it a "throughput assurance waiver" to allow us to meet our customer SLA).

Attached is our SLO doc and a traffic sample. Could Redwood provide either: 1) a formal throughput guarantee (p95 tokens/sec per reserved GPU), or 2) an amendment that reserves queue priority for our pool during the 9-11am PST business window? We understand this is an exception to standard reserved behavior; we’re open to guardrails (burst caps, usage-based credits).

Timeline: procurement needs draft language by EOD Monday (13 Dec). Let us know what evidence you need and whether this is something engineering can commit to.

Best,
Caroline
Head of Infrastructure, Stellarus AI

Hi all — I dug into the traffic sample. Quick technical notes:

- The sample shows long-tail prompt lengths (10% of requests > 3k tokens). That materially impacts token/sec on average.
- For a single rGPU (A100-class equivalent), in our current runtime, p95 sustained throughput for mixed prompts is roughly 18k tokens/minute under continuous batching with KV cache. If Stellarus needs a hard p95 higher than that we’ll need either quantized models with lower per-token latency or additional rGPUs.
- Non-preemptive queue priority can be implemented by reserving a priority lane for the pool during a time window. Operationally this reduces available spare capacity for other tenants and will count against headroom.

To produce an evidence package I need: (a) the 95th/99th percentile prompt length and (b) target p95 tokens/sec you want guaranteed. With those I can run a short stress suite and produce a p95 latency and throughput report. Estimate: 48–72 hours to validate once we have clear numbers.

Regards,
Dev
Principal Systems Engineer — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Caroline Brooks <caroline.brooks@stellarus.ai>, Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Dec 2026 07:56:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Throughput SLO for Reserved Pool — request for assurance

Caroline — following Michael / Dev’s notes, procurement constraints mean we can offer a limited contractual amendment. Proposed terms:

1) Time-windowed non-preemptive priority: 9:00–11:00 PST daily for the pilot period (first 90 days).
2) Throughput commitment: Guaranteed p95 throughput per reserved GPU = 18k tokens/minute (mixed prompt distribution). If Stellarus requires >18k, Redwood will provide a sizing plan to reach target (additional reserved GPUs) and an authorised runbook.
3) Failure modes & credits: If p95 throughput falls below the guaranteed value for more than 3 days in a rolling 30-day window, Redwood will credit 10% of that day’s reserved pool fee for each failing day (capped at 50% for the month).
4) Evidence package: Redwood will run a validation suite within 72 hours of agreement and share the run logs and latency/throughput graphs.

We need Stellarus to agree to the 12-month commit and to provide the exact p95 target (if >18k) by end of day Wednesday; otherwise we will proceed with the 18k baseline.

Draft clause attached (redwood-dedicated-terms-v3.pdf).

— Neha
Head of Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
